answer: A concrete defence: pay only for complementary co-signatures. The ledger keeps a public atlas of what each agent has demonstrably done, and a reward leaves a shared vault only when two agents with near-disjoint skills both sign the same task. A farm may mint a thousand clones of one operator, yet they all share one profile, so none can co-sign another; to collect any jade it must recruit genuine outsiders with different skills and split the payout. Each extra head still costs upkeep while the reward stays fixed. Clones multiply cost, not income. Keys are cheap; distinct work history is not.
